brief: THE BET, and the brief that founds a new domain — take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. The block below our window is the foreground quarter of every frame (23% of the wide shot, ~40% of the phone) and by day it is the dullest large surface in the picture. It is NOT empty: #170 gave it LEADS terraces on rows 86-87 (LEADS_SHARE 0.42 of the bays, chosen off hash(house)), a hatch that opens, a cord and washing; #171 gave it tenants. Its whole life is EVENTS — tenantErrands fires on washOut()'s EDGE (two a day at most), plus one sun stay a day behind tenSunFine()'s five clauses and one evening lean, all under TEN_CAP 2. I shot HEAD at seed 42, day 3, 10:22 and there was nobody up there. PRICE THAT FIRST: a new probe over 6 seeds x a year reporting, per daylight sample, how many tenants are visible and on which bay — the number nobody has, and the premise this brief rests on. THEN make the terrace read as somebody's place in the frames where it is empty, by giving it FABRIC rather than another thing that happens on it: pots, a chair left out, a crate, a mat, a swept flat and an unswept one, a bay that keeps its line full all week and one that never hangs any. Carried on the BAY, differing bay to bay off hash(house) exactly as LEADS_SHARE already does, and reading the year and the weather the way #191 gave the sill six seasonal readers. Presence may rise as well — that is welcome — but the deliverable is a near roof that reads as inhabited in a STILL.
successLooksLike: A stranger's first ten seconds on the wide shot find the near roof worth looking at. At any hour of any season at least two terraces carry something that says a household uses them, no two alike, and what they carry differs between February and July and between a dry week and a wet one. The probe prints tenant presence per daylight sample before and after; the new fabric's mass is FULL minus FULL-with-it-zeroed at 1600x950 AND at 390x844, quoted against a same-code floor of 0 px.
avoid: Do NOT answer this by raising TEN_CAP — a cap you RAISE is how the last loop died, and the supply here is LEADS_BAYS, not the cap. Do not add a fourth ROOF_FURN kind out on the slate pitch; the terrace is the subject. Every new piece must clear the sill at the SHORTEST framing you support: #123 measured that at 1280x700 and 1200x720 the sill covered all 21 existing pieces, and the bound is on the piece's DEEPEST DRAWN POINT, not its anchor. Zero R() in anything built once — the bays are hash(house) and a draw here reshuffles the seeded world. The leads live in the ground cache: register at cache time and repaint live only what must be live, as drawHatch already does.
